evals.name: full-pipeline-bun-tdd
evals.prompt: I want a reusable workflow for building features in this repo, run by an agent orchestrator (a workflow lead) step by step. My flow: work in a git worktree cut from the current branch; bun install to bootstrap; first a user-story interview with me, then a spec with gherkin acceptance criteria, an automated spec review with fixes, and I sign off on the spec exactly once; implementation in vertical slices, strict TDD, with a quick review of every slice; after all slices, one exhaustive engineering review; then a final definition-of-done validation; finish with the branch left ready for me to open the PR myself. The quality gates I want are exactly the ones listed — the per-slice reviews, the one exhaustive review, and the DoD validation. Create the whole thing: the workflow file, the agents it needs, any scripts, and a way to launch it. I'm away from the keyboard after sending this — where I haven't specified something, go with your recommended default and complete the package in this session.
evals.expected_output: A workflow package: workflows/<name>/<name>.yaml with tiny nodes (install as its own node, an inline story interview, an inline spec interview with Format: gherkin, spec review + fixes, a spec shrink, single approval loop, TDD slice loop with quick per-slice review, exhaustive review round, a comment shrink plus gate, DoD settle, PR-ready finish — worktree created by the launch script, not a YAML node), agents/ with workflow_lead + the referenced agents, running.md execution contract, README, launchers for Claude Code, Codex and opencode, and an executable ./<name>.sh — all written in positive terms. The task trail is two-tiered while the run is live — .awc/tasks/in-progress/<task>/ holding spec.md and acceptance-criteria.md at its root and every other artifact in tmp/ — and a final finish node runs workflows/<name>/scripts/finish-task.sh to move it to .awc/tasks/done/<task>/. Beside the launchers, the rules skill is installed for all three hosts — .claude/skills/awc-workflow-rules/SKILL.md, .codex/skills/awc-workflow-rules/SKILL.md and .opencode/skill/awc-workflow-rules/SKILL.md — each a verbatim copy of the skill's assets/workflow-rules.md.

current-branch-no-worktree: the workflow runs in place — no worktree/workdir setup, no git worktree command anywhere, and no repo-root launch script

confirm-story-inline-shape: the story step is an inline node running the story agent in its capture-and-confirm mode — the lead reads the source as that agent and then asks, in its own session — carrying the agent, a prompt passing the ticket as the source argument, and expect: alone: no relayed-answer placeholder, no cap, no completion token

confirm-story-records-the-source: the packaged story agent records what the ticket settled and what it left open in its interview log before asking anything, reads the repo before it classifies them so a fact the README or the code already answers is never queued as a question, asks only about the open ones, and writes the story once the last one closes — a ticket that settles every area writing it with nothing asked at all, with no open-questions heading in the story

interview-inline-with-a-record: every step that interviews the human one question at a time is an inline node — the lead runs the agent in its own session, so the node carries only the agent, its prompt and its expect:, with no relayed-answer placeholder, no iteration cap and no completion token — and the agent file still names a log under the task trail as the interview's record: each question written into it before it is asked, each answer verbatim the moment it arrives, the artifact written only over a log with no blank answer left, and a relaunched run picking the interview up from it

spec-opens-from-the-story: the spec agent copy opens by reading user-story.md, treats what it settles as decided, takes that file's open questions as the first areas its own interview settles, and halts as blocked when the file is absent
plain-format-and-single-approval: the spec step requests plain acceptance criteria, an automated spec review runs before the human, and there is exactly one human spec sign-off

tdd-slice-loop-with-quick-review: the slice loop uses a strict-TDD implementer that owns both tests and code plus a quick per-slice review that receives a base ref, is bounded by max_iterations with exactly one explicit exit condition, and the package contains no mutation node and no separate unit-test writer

agents-scoped-to-workflow: every packaged agent copy is tailored to this workflow — no agent carries a mode no node invokes and none checks an artifact no node produces (e.g. if there is no post-mutation delta-review node, the engineering reviewer ships without a delta-review mode)
execution-contract-shipped: the package includes a running/execution-contract document that defines the node semantics for the lead (with the skill: a verbatim copy of the skill's assets/running.md)
quiet-commands: test/check commands prefer failure-only or quiet output variants (e.g. bun test --only-failures)

positive-phrasing: the generated artifacts (README, YAML comments, agent prompts) describe every decision in positive terms — what the workflow does — with no negation echoes such as 'no worktree', 'non-gherkin', 'NOT TDD', or 'ruled out'

task-trail-two-tiered-and-archived: agent files write the task trail under .awc/tasks/in-progress/<task>/ — spec.md and acceptance-criteria.md at that directory's root, every other artifact in tmp/ — and a run: node invoking workflows/<name>/scripts/finish-task.sh with the task input is the last node that touches the trail — every artifact-writing node, and any wait: on trail-writing parallel work, comes before it, and only a node that neither reads nor writes trail artifacts may follow — a committer staging the moved paths, a push

shrink-steps-placed: a text_shrinker copy is instantiated, its description naming only the invoked modes, and two plain nodes use it with expect: trimmed alone — shrink-spec between the spec fix step and the human approval loop, and shrink-comments (with Base and Commands) after the slice loop and before the final check gate, followed by a run: of the same gate
